stories.headline: SpaceX targets record $75B IPO at $135 per share, $1.75T valuation

key_facts.fact: SpaceX plans to sell 555.6 million shares at $135 each to raise $75 billion, an unusual move that fixes a price before the investor roadshow
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX plans to raise $75 billion in its initial public offering by selling 555.6 million shares at a target price of $135 per share

key_facts.fact: Target valuation is $1.75 trillion in what would be the largest IPO in history; the offering is structured as all-primary with no insider sales
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket and satellite company, plans to target a valuation of $1.75 trillion in its blockbuster initial public offering, which will consist entirely of new shares

key_facts.fact: Roadshow begins Thursday June 4; SpaceX aims to debut on Nasdaq under ticker SPCX as early as June 12
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's roadshow begins on Thursday... SpaceX is aiming to trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol 'SPCX.' The debut is expected on June 12

key_facts.fact: Musk will be required to hold his SpaceX shares for 366 days after the IPO under a lockup; greenshoe option set at 15%
key_facts.excerpt: Musk will be required to hold his SpaceX shares for 366 days after the IPO, one of the sources said, a signal to investors of his commitment to the company

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BofA Securities, Citigroup and JPMorgan are joint book-running managers
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, BofA Securities, Citigroup and J.P. Morgan are the joint book-running managers for the offering

stories.headline: US sanctions Nobitex and three other Iranian crypto exchanges over IRGC links

key_facts.fact: The US Treasury's OFAC designated Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin and Ramzinex on June 2 for facilitating terrorist financing and sanctions evasion
key_facts.excerpt: The Treasury's Office of Foreign Asset Control announced that Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin and Ramzinex, as well as some of these exchanges' executives, were being added to its global Specially Designated Nationals list

key_facts.fact: Treasury alleges Nobitex processed more than 50% of all Iranian digital asset inflows in 2025 and facilitated IRGC-linked transactions including ransomware payments
key_facts.excerpt: The Treasury Department alleges Nobitex processed more than 50% of all Iranian digital asset inflows in 2025 and facilitated payments tied to Iran's terrorist activities, sanctions evasion efforts, and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-linked transactions

key_facts.fact: Nobitex handled roughly $5 billion in transactions from 2025 to March 2026, per TRM Labs
key_facts.excerpt: Nobitex handled roughly US$5 billion (S$6.4 billion) in transactions from 2025 to March 2026, according to TRM Labs

key_facts.fact: Treasury also sanctioned Nobitex's three co-founders and current CEO; Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his department has seized roughly $1 billion in crypto from Iranian wallets since the war began
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that his department had seized around $1 billion in crypto from Iranian exchanges and wallets since the beginning of the war against Iran

key_facts.fact: Treasury alleges Nobitex helped Iran move assets out of the country after US bombing began and aided the Central Bank of Iran in accessing stablecoins to prop up the rial
key_facts.excerpt: [Nobitex] also helped the Central Bank of Iran access hundreds of millions of dollars in stablecoins used to prop up the plummeting value of the Iranian rial

stories.headline: Iran fires missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain; US strikes Qeshm Island in response

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said Iran fired ballistic missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain on June 2 that failed or were shot down; US responded with strikes on an Iranian ground control station on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military said Tuesday that Iran fired missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain that failed or were shot down, and that the U.S. launched strikes on an Iranian facility in response... U.S. Central Command said it responded with strikes on an Iranian military ground control station on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Iran's Fars and Tasnim news agencies reported Tehran stopped communicating with mediators about extending the US-Iran ceasefire; Trump disputed this and said talks were continuing
key_facts.excerpt: The attacks happened after Iran stopped communicating with mediators about extending a ceasefire in the war with the U.S. and Israel, according to reports Tuesday from two semiofficial Iranian news agencies. President Donald Trump disputed the claim and said talks were continuing

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose above $97 a barrel on June 3, a third consecutive session of gains, as the geopolitical risk premium climbed
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures climbed above $97 per barrel on Wednesday, marking a third consecutive session of gains as ongoing uncertainty surrounding US-Iran peace negotiations and renewed conflict in the Middle East continued to support a geopolitical risk premium in oil markets

key_facts.fact: Israel kept up strikes on southern Lebanon on June 2 despite a partial truce; Lebanon's Civil Defense said six people were killed in a strike on Marwaniyeh village
key_facts.excerpt: Israel continued to launch its own strikes on Lebanon, with the Lebanese Civil Defense saying on its Facebook page Tuesday that six people had been killed in an Israeli strike Monday night in the village of Marwaniyeh in southern Lebanon

key_facts.fact: Trump told ABC News he expected an agreement to extend the ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within the next week
key_facts.excerpt: He also told ABC News that he expected an agreement to extend the ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within the next week

stories.headline: Drone strike kills seven on bus in Russian-held Donetsk; Russia hits Ukraine with 198 drones overnight

key_facts.fact: Seven people were killed and eleven injured early Wednesday June 3 in a drone attack on a passenger bus traveling between Moscow and Simferopol in Russian-controlled Donetsk, per Kremlin-installed leader Denis Pushilin
key_facts.excerpt: Seven people have been killed and 11 others injured in a drone attack on a passenger bus travelling through a Russia-controlled part of Ukraine... Denis Pushilin, the Kremlin-installed leader of Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region, said the bus was hit in the early hours of Wednesday as it was travelling between Moscow and Simferopol

key_facts.fact: Russia launched 198 attack drones against Ukraine overnight June 2-3; Ukrainian air defenses downed 189 of them; impacts recorded at seven locations
key_facts.excerpt: Russia launched 198 attack drones against Ukraine from multiple directions during the night of June 3... air defenses had shot down or suppressed 189 enemy UAVs

key_facts.fact: Russia downed more than 350 drones overnight on its side, including at least 50 over the Leningrad region, which from Wednesday hosts the St Petersburg International Economic Forum with delegations from 130+ countries
key_facts.excerpt: Russia downed more than 350 drones overnight, according to Russian officials. At least 50 drones were downed over the Leningrad region northwest of Moscow... The region includes the city of St Petersburg, which from Wednesday will host the annual International Economic Forum

key_facts.fact: ISW says Russia's June 2 strike (656 drones + 73 missiles) was designed to exploit Ukrainian Patriot missile shortages and divert attention from setbacks; Russia used cluster munitions and double-tap strikes on emergency responders
key_facts.excerpt: Russia launched its massive June 2 attack on Ukraine to exploit shortages of Patriot missiles and divert attention from its inability to protect Russia's deep rear areas... ISW notes that Russia's use of cluster munitions and double-tap strikes on emergency responders demonstrates a Russian tactic aimed at killing as many civilians in Ukraine as possible

key_facts.fact: Zelensky warned that intelligence suggests Russia could launch a new large-scale attack on the night of June 3
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said it was a 'brutal strike' and warned that intelligence suggested Russia could launch a new assault for the second night in a row. 'According to our intelligence, another large-scale attack may occur tonight,' he said

stories.headline: Bitcoin slides below $67K after Strategy's first BTC sale since 2022 spooks market

key_facts.fact: Bitcoin fell about 8.58% to near $67,206 after Strategy disclosed selling 32 BTC for $2.5 million between May 26-31 at an average of $77,135 per coin
key_facts.excerpt: Bitcoin slumped 8.58% to trade near $67,206... MicroStrategy disclosed in a Form 8-K that it sold 32 BTC for roughly $2.5 million. The sale ran from May 26 to May 31

key_facts.fact: MSTR closed down 9.95% on June 2 and has lost nearly 70% over the past year; market cap fell from above $160B to roughly $48B
key_facts.excerpt: MSTR closed down 9.95% on the day and has shed nearly 70% over the past year. Its market capitalization has fallen from above $160 billion to roughly $48 billion

key_facts.fact: Strategy still holds 843,706 BTC at an average cost of $75,699, leaving the position with more than $6 billion in unrealized losses; the 32-coin sale was just 0.0038% of holdings
key_facts.excerpt: Strategy still held 843,706 bitcoin as of May 31 at an average purchase price of $75,699, leaving the sale price above its cost basis... the sale accounted for just 0.0038% of the company's holdings

key_facts.fact: Proceeds will fund dividend payments on Strategy's STRC perpetual preferred stock; STRC has slipped below its $100 peg
key_facts.excerpt: The sale, the company's first disclosed net bitcoin disposal, will be used to pay the dividend on the company's STRC perpetual preferred stock

key_facts.fact: Bitcoin ETFs posted their 10th consecutive day of net outflows on May 29, the longest streak ever; the Crypto Fear & Greed Index hit 23 in 'Extreme Fear' territory
key_facts.excerpt: Bitcoin ETFs on Friday posted their 10th day in a row — and longest streak ever — of net outflows

key_facts.fact: Almost $1.5 billion in crypto liquidations triggered in 24 hours; bitcoin sits more than 42% below its all-time high above $126,000
key_facts.excerpt: Bitcoin is more than 42% from its all-time high over $126,000

stories.headline: GitLab cuts 14% of staff and exits 22 countries in 'agentic era' restructuring

key_facts.fact: GitLab is cutting roughly 350 full-time employees, about 14% of its workforce, and exiting 22 countries to shrink its geographic footprint by about 37%
key_facts.excerpt: GitLab is cutting about 14% of its full-time workforce, roughly 350 people, and pulling out of 22 countries... The country exits will shrink GitLab's geographic footprint by about 37%

key_facts.fact: Restructuring will incur $30-35M in pre-tax charges, primarily severance and termination costs, with about $19M hitting Q2 FY27
key_facts.excerpt: It estimates that it will incur approximately $30 million to $35 million in pre-tax restructuring charges, consisting primarily of one-time severance, employee termination benefit costs, and retention costs... approximately $19 million is expected to be incurred in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027

key_facts.fact: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to $264M, 4 points above guidance; non-GAAP operating income reached $38M at a 14% margin
key_facts.excerpt: GitLab delivered a robust first quarter for fiscal 2027, with revenue of $264 million, up 23% year-over-year and 4 points above its guidance. Non-GAAP operating income reached $38 million at a 14% margin

key_facts.fact: GitLab Duo Agent Platform contributed more net new ARR in Q1 than Duo Pro and Duo Enterprise combined in any prior quarter, ending Q1 with paid consumption run rate of nearly $20M
key_facts.excerpt: GitLab Duo Agent Platform... contributed more net new ARR in its first quarter than Duo Pro and Duo Enterprise combined in any prior quarter, and ended Q1 with a paid consumption run rate of nearly $20 million

key_facts.fact: CEO Bill Staples framed the layoffs as 'Act Two' restructuring; up to three layers of management will be removed and savings reinvested in R&D and AI tooling
key_facts.excerpt: The Act Two plan, detailed in a public letter from Staples and elaborated on the call, will cut approximately 350 positions—14% of the workforce as of January 31, 2026—and exit 22 countries... Up to three layers of management will be removed to flatten the organization

key_facts.fact: GitLab shares fell 5.83% after the announcement; full-year revenue guidance raised to $1.112-$1.118B
key_facts.excerpt: GitLab GTLB -5.83 %decrease; red down pointing triangle is cutting 350 full-time employees, about 14% of its total workforce

stories.headline: FDA approves Otsuka's sibeprenlimab (Voyxact) for IgA nephropathy after 51% proteinuria cut

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved sibeprenlimab-szsi (Voyxact; Otsuka) to reduce proteinuria in adults with IgA nephropathy, based on interim Phase 3 VISIONARY trial data
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA has approved sibeprenlimab-szsi (Voyxact; Otsuka) to reduce proteinuria in adults who have immunoglobulin A nephropathy(IgAN), based on an interim analysis of data from the phase 3 VISIONARY trial

key_facts.fact: Treatment is a 400 mg subcutaneous self-injection via prefilled syringe every 4 weeks at home
key_facts.excerpt: Administration is via a prefilled syringe for subcutaneous self-injection every 4 weeks at home. The recommended single dose is 400 mg

key_facts.fact: VISIONARY trial showed a 51.2% reduction in proteinuria vs placebo at 9 months (p<0.0001); 510 patients enrolled across the cohort
key_facts.excerpt: Data used to support this approval show a 9-month proteinuria reduction of 50% vs 2% in those who received placebo... A prespecified interim analysis of VISIONARY data... showing a 51.2% reduction (P < .0001) in proteinuria

key_facts.fact: Safety profile showed 76.3% of treated patients experienced any treatment-emergent adverse event vs 84.5% on placebo; serious AE rates were 3.9% vs 5.4%
key_facts.excerpt: Safety data also were positive, showing 76.3% of treated patients compared with 84.5% of patients who received placebo experienced any treatment-emergent adverse event (AE), with serious AE rates of 3.9% and 5.4%, respectively

key_facts.fact: A confirmatory trial is still needed to determine if sibeprenlimab can slow kidney function decline at 24 months for ongoing approval
key_facts.excerpt: A confirmatory trial is still needed to determine if sibeprenlimab can slow kidney function decline over the long term (ie, at 24 months), as well as for ongoing approval of this new indication

sources.title: FDA Approves Sibeprenlimab for Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy
